text: Do you know the Space Shuttle came home from space with no engine running? It landed as a glider.
This is the real Discovery, laser scanned by the Smithsonian. It flew to space thirty-nine times. More than any other spacecraft.
Thirty-seven metres long, with wings almost twenty-four metres wide.
Coming home, the heat outside reached one thousand six hundred and fifty degrees Celsius.
But its aluminium body could not go above one hundred and seventy-five degrees.
So it wore twenty-four thousand tiles, made of silica, from almost pure quartz sand.
They were so light and fragile, you could crush one with your hand.
The nose and the front edges of the wings got the worst of it. They were made of reinforced carbon-carbon.
Black tiles underneath, where it was hottest. White on top, where it was cooler.
Then, no power at all. On the final approach, it moved only about four and a half metres forward, for every metre it dropped.
That's a steep dive for something the size of an airliner.
After thirty-nine flights, about eighteen thousand of its tiles were still the originals.
